# Exact read-only Kernel byte fixture

This is executable-code content stored as `.txt` exclusively for the existing
content-identical Kernel alias-denial assertion. Never import, load or execute it.
It is not a complete Kernel, runtime closure, executable dependency or live fixture.

- Upstream: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
- Fixed commit: `639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84`
- CLI package: `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.2.0-rc.2, `apps/cli/package.json`, license MIT.
- Original generated entry: `apps/cli/lib/bin.js`, built from `apps/cli/src/bin.ts`
  and local CLI modules through the upstream `apps/cli/tsdown.config.ts`.
- Local materialization manifest records that upstream commit and entry checksum.
  The generated entry is not a Git blob at that commit; repeat-build byte identity
  has not been established. This fixture preserves the audited output verbatim.
- Payload: **11,697 bytes**, SHA-256
  `1A03DEE18683483FF6A1B27B2A1E650230DA6BCCA9A0F55F7D81B3308C3F307F`.
- Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek. Full upstream MIT notice accompanies these bytes.
  The CLI package's MIT declaration covers its bundled CLI source. External
  dependencies are imports, not included dependency packages; this fixture does
  not grant or assert permission to redistribute a complete runtime closure.

The test-only resource preparer copies just this entry and renders two pinned
text literals to the existing ignored test paths **before Guard initialization**.
That retains the Guard's existing hash-alias refusal; it does not register or
authorize a Kernel launch. Existing matching files are read, never overwritten.
Fresh-checkout runners with an outer Guard preload must prepare resources first
in a separately reviewed preparation step, then start the guarded test process.
No materializer, dependency installation, network or PowerShell is invoked.

Local candidate inclusion is authorized by the Windows-first convergence decision.
Remote source transfer, GitHub upload and real Kernel execution remain unauthorized.
